subject: TerraHealth RFI: segmentation, egress controls and evidence request
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@terrahealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: TerraHealth RFI: segmentation, egress controls and evidence request

Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our procurement security review we need a short RFI packet focused on network segmentation, tenant egress controls, and supporting evidence. Specifically we are asking for: 

- A network diagram showing inference zones (control plane vs. inference compute), sidecar placement, VPC peering, and NAT/bastion points.
- A short threat-model summary that explains how lateral movement is limited between tenants and how egress is constrained.
- Sample artifacts: a sanitized VPC flow log sample, KMS policy snippet showing customer key separation, and any console screenshots that demonstrate peering/route table constructs.
- Retention policy for flow logs and audit logs and where logs are stored.

Can you provide a packaged response by EOD Thursday (2028-05-03)? If we need an NDA or redaction agreement before sharing logs, please advise.

Regards,
Elena Park
Head of Security, TerraHealth

[TerraHealth logo]

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask. We can compile the packet you outlined. Proposed plan: 

1) High-level diagram + short threat-model summary (1 page each) — attached diagram v3 + 1-page threat notes.
2) Evidence artifacts: sanitized VPC flow log sample, KMS policy snippet, and screenshots of VPC peering/route tables. We will sanitize PII and customer-identifying metadata per our evidence redaction policy.
3) Retention & controls section with links to our audit evidence repository.

We can deliver the packet by 2028-05-03 EOD PST. If TerraHealth requires an NDA prior to receiving sanitized logs, say the word and I’ll circulate our standard mutual NDA.

Attaching a draft network diagram (first pass) for your review.

Thanks — I’ll follow up after Marcus and Security have reviewed.

Best,
Monica Patel

Thanks Marcus — taking this on. Deliverables prepared below and attached. Please review and let me know if TerraHealth needs further detail.

Summary of controls (short):
- Topology: customer inference workloads run in isolated tenant pools. We support both: a) VPC-per-tenant (private deployment) and b) logically multi-tenant GPU pools with strict namespace and sidecar isolation (host-networking disabled by default). Sidecar proxies enforce egress allowlists per-tenant.
- Egress controls: sidecar-level allowlists + NAT gateways in controlled subnets. No direct public IPs on inference hosts. Transit VPC and centralized egress firewall for outbound filtering and TLS inspection (if customer requests it).
- Key management: Customer-managed keys (CMKs) supported. Attached is a minimal KMS policy snippet showing explicit separation of ARNs for tenant-specific keys.
- Logging & retention: VPC Flow Logs and control-plane audit logs retained for 365 days by default for Managed/Hosted tiers; Dedicated/Private can be configured per contract. Logs stored in encrypted object storage with access guarded by RBAC and key separation.

Attachments included (sanitized):
- redwood_network_slice_diagram_v3.svg (annotated)
- egres_control_playbook_v1.2.pdf (playbook with operating steps and runbook)
- sanitized_vpc_flowlogs_sample.csv (example rows with IPs redacted)
- kms_key_policy_snippet.txt

Notes on redaction: we remove/customer-hash all tenant identifiers before sharing. If TerraHealth requires unredacted artifacts for an in-person audit, we can provide them under a scoped NDA and physical audit procedure.

Evidence repo: https://drive.redwood.com/terrahealth/rfi/evidence

Kimberly Park
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: egres_control_playbook_v1.2.pdf]
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-01T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TerraHealth RFI: segmentation, egress controls and evidence request

Hi Elena / TerraHealth team — attached is the requested packet. Quick answers to your numbered asks below, followed by next steps.

1) Diagram: attached (redwood_network_slice_diagram_v3.svg). Diagram notes: control plane (control.redwood.internal) is segregated from inference pools; sidecars run per-pod and perform tenant-level egress allowlisting.

2) Threat model summary: see page 2 of the attached playbook (egres_control_playbook_v1.2.pdf). High-level mitigations include strict RBAC, sidecar-enforced outbound policies, and kernel hardening on inference hosts.

3) Sample artifacts: sanitized VPC Flow Logs attached (sanitized_vpc_flowlogs_sample.csv) and KMS snippet (kms_key_policy_snippet.txt). All logs have tenant identifiers hashed; full artifacts can be provided under NDA.

4) Retention: default 365 days for flow logs and audit logs in Hosted; Dedicated contracts can extend retention and direct log export to customer-owned storage.

Next steps: if useful, Kimberly is available to walk through the packet on a 30-minute call. We can also execute your mutual NDA if TerraHealth wants unredacted artifacts for an onsite review. Proposed times: 2028-05-04 09:00 or 2028-05-04 14:00 PT.

Let me know which slot works and whether you want the NDA sent over.

Best regards,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
